paracetamol.description: Used to relieve mild to moderate pain and reduce fever. Works by blocking pain signals in the brain.

ibuprofen.description: Reduces pain, inflammation, and fever. Works by blocking COX enzymes that produce prostaglandins.

aspirin.description: Used for pain relief, fever reduction, and to prevent blood clots. Low-dose aspirin is used for heart attack prevention.

amoxicillin.description: Treats bacterial infections of the ear, nose, throat, urinary tract, and skin. Does NOT work against viruses.

azithromycin.description: Treats bacterial infections including respiratory, skin, ear, and sexually transmitted infections.

metformin.description: First-line treatment for Type 2 diabetes. Lowers blood sugar by reducing glucose production in the liver and improving insulin sensitivity.

amlodipine.description: Treats high blood pressure and chest pain (angina). Relaxes blood vessels to improve blood flow.

atorvastatin.description: Lowers LDL (bad) cholesterol and triglycerides. Reduces risk of heart attack and stroke.
warnings: Take at the same time daily

omeprazole.description: Reduces stomach acid production. Treats acid reflux (GERD), ulcers, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.

pantoprazole.description: Reduces stomach acid. Used for GERD, erosive esophagitis, and peptic ulcers.
warnings: Long-term use may cause magnesium deficiency

cetirizine.description: Treats allergies, hay fever, and hives. Relieves sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes.

montelukast.description: Prevents asthma attacks and relieves seasonal allergy symptoms. Blocks leukotrienes that cause airway swelling.
warnings: FDA warning: may cause mood/behavior changes

warfarin.description: Prevents blood clots in veins and arteries. Used after heart valve replacement, DVT, pulmonary embolism, and atrial fibrillation.

clopidogrel.description: Prevents blood clots after heart attack, stroke, or stent placement. Works by stopping platelets from sticking together.
warnings: Do not stop without doctor's advice

losartan.description: Treats high blood pressure and protects kidneys in diabetic patients. Relaxes blood vessels.

metoprolol.description: Treats high blood pressure, chest pain (angina), and heart failure. Slows heart rate and reduces heart workload.
warnings: May mask low blood sugar symptoms in diabetics

ciprofloxacin.description: Treats urinary tract infections, respiratory infections, and gastrointestinal infections.
warnings: FDA black box warning for tendon rupture

diclofenac.description: Treats pain, inflammation, and swelling from arthritis, sprains, and menstrual cramps.
warnings: Not for long-term use without monitoring

ranitidine.description: Reduces stomach acid production. Used for heartburn, acid reflux, and stomach ulcers.
warnings: FDA recall in 2020 for NDMA contamination — check with pharmacist for availability

levothyroxine.description: Replaces thyroid hormone in hypothyroidism. Regulates metabolism, energy, and body temperature.
warnings: Take on empty stomach 30-60 min before breakfast

salbutamol.description: Quick-relief inhaler for asthma and COPD. Opens airways within minutes during an attack.
warnings: If using more than 3 times/week, see doctor

prednisolone.description: Treats inflammation, allergies, asthma, and autoimmune conditions. Suppresses the immune system.
warnings: Long-term use causes serious side effects

glimepiride.description: Lowers blood sugar by stimulating the pancreas to produce more insulin. Used in Type 2 diabetes.

telmisartan.description: Treats high blood pressure. Protects heart and kidneys in high-risk patients.

domperidone.description: Treats nausea and vomiting. Speeds up stomach emptying.

dextromethorphan.description: Suppresses dry cough by acting on the cough center in the brain. Does not treat underlying cause.
warnings: Do not use for productive (wet) cough

tramadol.description: Treats moderate to severe pain. Works on opioid receptors and inhibits serotonin/norepinephrine reuptake.

fluoxetine.description: Treats depression, OCD, panic disorder, and bulimia. Increases serotonin levels in the brain.
warnings: FDA black box warning: increased suicidality in young adults

hydroxychloroquine.description: Treats malaria, rheumatoid arthritis, and lupus. Modulates the immune system.
warnings: Regular eye exams required (retinal damage risk)

gabapentin.description: Treats nerve pain (neuropathy), seizures, and restless leg syndrome.
warnings: Do not stop suddenly (may cause seizures)

fexofenadine.description: Treats seasonal allergies and hives without causing drowsiness. A safer alternative to older antihistamines.

cefixime.description: Treats urinary tract infections, ear infections, throat infections, and gonorrhea.

ofloxacin.description: Treats UTIs, respiratory infections, skin infections, and certain STIs.
warnings: FDA black box warning for tendon rupture

levofloxacin.description: Treats pneumonia, sinusitis, UTIs, and skin infections. More potent than ofloxacin.
warnings: FDA black box warning for tendon rupture and nerve damage

doxycycline.description: Treats acne, respiratory infections, UTIs, malaria prevention, and tick-borne diseases.
warnings: Avoid lying down for 30 min after taking

amitriptyline.description: Treats depression, nerve pain, migraine prevention, and insomnia at low doses.
warnings: Can cause heart rhythm changes at high doses

sertraline.description: Treats depression, anxiety, OCD, PTSD, and panic disorder. Generally well-tolerated.

escitalopram.description: Treats depression and generalized anxiety disorder. One of the best-tolerated SSRIs.
warnings: Can cause QT prolongation at high doses

clonazepam.description: Treats seizures, panic disorder, and anxiety. Works by enhancing GABA activity in the brain.

alprazolam.description: Treats anxiety and panic attacks. Fast-acting but high potential for dependence.
warnings: Never mix with alcohol or opioids

rosuvastatin.description: Lowers LDL cholesterol and triglycerides. More potent than atorvastatin at lower doses.

sitagliptin.description: Treats Type 2 diabetes by increasing incretin hormones that stimulate insulin release after meals.
warnings: Dose adjustment needed in kidney disease

insulin_glargine.description: Provides 24-hour basal insulin coverage for Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes.

lisinopril.description: Treats high blood pressure and heart failure. Protects kidneys in diabetic patients.
warnings: Dry cough is common and harmless

furosemide.description: Removes excess fluid from the body. Treats swelling (edema) in heart failure, liver disease, and kidney disease.
warnings: Can cause hearing damage at very high IV doses

spironolactone.description: Treats heart failure, high blood pressure, and fluid retention. Also used for hormonal acne and PCOS.

hydrochlorothiazide.description: Treats high blood pressure and fluid retention. Often combined with ARBs or ACE inhibitors.

nifedipine.description: Treats high blood pressure and Raynaud's phenomenon. Relaxes blood vessels.

carvedilol.description: Treats heart failure and high blood pressure. Blocks both alpha and beta receptors.
warnings: Stand up slowly to avoid dizziness

phenytoin.description: Controls seizures (epilepsy). Stabilizes electrical activity in the brain.
warnings: Narrow therapeutic window (blood level monitoring needed)

sodium_valproate.description: Treats epilepsy, bipolar disorder, and migraine prevention.
warnings: Do NOT use in pregnancy (birth defects)

pioglitazone.description: Treats Type 2 diabetes by improving insulin sensitivity in muscles and fat tissue.

aceclofenac.description: Treats pain and inflammation from arthritis, dental pain, and musculoskeletal conditions.
warnings: Avoid in heart, kidney, or liver disease

etoricoxib.description: Treats arthritis pain, gout attacks, and dental pain. Causes fewer stomach problems than traditional NSAIDs.
warnings: Higher cardiovascular risk than other NSAIDs

rabeprazole.description: Reduces stomach acid. Treats acid reflux, GERD, peptic ulcers, and H. pylori infection.
warnings: Long-term use may cause bone loss and B12 deficiency

interactions.description: Greatly increases risk of serious bleeding. Aspirin inhibits platelet function while warfarin blocks clotting factors. Combined effect can cause life-threatening hemorrhage.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination unless specifically prescribed by cardiologist. Seek immediate medical advice.

interactions.description: NSAIDs increase bleeding risk and can cause GI ulcers. Combined with warfarin, risk of GI hemorrhage increases 3-6 times.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination. Use paracetamol for pain instead.

interactions.description: High-dose or prolonged paracetamol use may increase INR and bleeding risk with warfarin.
interactions.recommendation: Safe in low doses for short periods. Monitor INR if using regularly.

interactions.description: Azithromycin may increase warfarin levels by inhibiting its metabolism, leading to elevated INR and bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely during and after antibiotic course.

interactions.description: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2 enzyme, increasing warfarin concentration and bleeding risk significantly.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR very closely. Consider dose reduction of warfarin.

interactions.description: Diclofenac increases GI bleeding risk and interferes with platelet function. Extremely dangerous with warfarin.
interactions.recommendation: AVOID. Use paracetamol for pain instead.

interactions.description: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing conversion of clopidogrel to its active form. May decrease antiplatelet effectiveness by 25-50%.
interactions.recommendation: Use pantoprazole instead of omeprazole with clopidogrel.

interactions.description: Dual antiplatelet therapy increases bleeding risk but is intentionally prescribed after heart stents. Monitor for signs of bleeding.
interactions.recommendation: Only use together if prescribed by cardiologist. Watch for unusual bruising or bleeding.

interactions.description: Ciprofloxacin can cause unpredictable blood sugar changes (both hypo and hyperglycemia) when combined with metformin.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood sugar closely during antibiotic course.

interactions.description: Combined use increases risk of hypoglycemia (dangerously low blood sugar). However, this is a common intentional combination in diabetes management.
interactions.recommendation: Often prescribed together. Monitor blood sugar regularly. Carry glucose tablets.

interactions.description: Ibuprofen can block aspirin's cardioprotective antiplatelet effect. Also increases risk of GI bleeding when both are used.
interactions.recommendation: If taking low-dose aspirin for heart protection, take it 30 minutes BEFORE ibuprofen. Avoid regular combined use.

interactions.description: Both are NSAIDs — combined use greatly increases risk of stomach ulcers and GI bleeding without additional pain benefit.
interactions.recommendation: AVOID using two NSAIDs together. Choose one.

interactions.description: Two NSAIDs together double the risk of GI bleeding and kidney damage without additional pain relief.
interactions.recommendation: NEVER combine two NSAIDs. Choose one and use at lowest effective dose.

interactions.description: NSAIDs reduce the blood-pressure-lowering effect of ARBs and increase risk of kidney damage, especially in dehydrated patients.
interactions.recommendation: Use paracetamol for pain instead. If NSAID necessary, use shortest course and monitor kidney function.

interactions.description: NSAIDs can reduce the blood-pressure-lowering effect of calcium channel blockers.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure. Use paracetamol if possible.

interactions.description: Both increase serotonin levels. Combined use can cause serotonin syndrome — a potentially fatal condition with symptoms including agitation, rapid heartbeat, high temperature, and seizures.
interactions.recommendation: AVOID combination. If pain management needed, use non-serotonergic alternatives.

interactions.description: SSRIs increase the risk of GI bleeding, especially when combined with NSAIDs.
interactions.recommendation: Consider adding a stomach protector (PPI) if both are necessary.

interactions.description: Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2C9, increasing warfarin levels and bleeding risk. SSRIs also impair platelet function independently.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely when starting or stopping fluoxetine.

interactions.description: Both increase serotonin. Fluoxetine also inhibits CYP2D6, slowing dextromethorphan metabolism. Risk of serotonin syndrome.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid cough syrups containing dextromethorphan while on fluoxetine.

interactions.description: Amlodipine increases atorvastatin blood levels by ~40%, increasing the risk of statin side effects (muscle pain, rhabdomyolysis).
interactions.recommendation: Limit atorvastatin to 20mg daily when combined with amlodipine.

interactions.description: Both lower blood pressure and heart rate. Combined use may cause excessive bradycardia (slow heart rate) or hypotension.
interactions.recommendation: Often used together intentionally. Monitor heart rate and blood pressure regularly.

interactions.description: PPIs reduce stomach acid needed for levothyroxine absorption, potentially decreasing thyroid hormone levels.
interactions.recommendation: Take levothyroxine at least 4 hours before omeprazole. Monitor TSH levels.

interactions.description: Metformin may slightly reduce TSH levels in hypothyroid patients on levothyroxine, potentially causing subclinical hyperthyroidism.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor TSH when starting metformin. Usually not clinically significant.

interactions.description: Both fluoroquinolones and corticosteroids increase the risk of tendon damage and rupture, especially in patients over 60.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination if possible. If necessary, monitor for tendon pain. Stop immediately if symptoms appear.

interactions.description: Both cause CNS depression. Combined use increases risk of sedation, respiratory depression, and dizziness.
interactions.recommendation: If used together, start with lower doses and monitor closely for excessive sedation.

interactions.description: Both can prolong the QT interval on ECG, increasing risk of dangerous heart arrhythmias (Torsades de Pointes).
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination. If necessary, obtain baseline ECG and monitor.

interactions.description: NSAIDs reduce the blood-pressure-lowering effect of ARBs and increase risk of acute kidney injury.
interactions.recommendation: Use paracetamol for pain instead. Ensure adequate hydration.

interactions.description: Both increase the risk of GI ulcers and bleeding. Combined risk is significantly higher than either alone.
interactions.recommendation: Add a PPI (like omeprazole) for stomach protection if both are necessary.

interactions.description: Corticosteroids raise blood sugar, counteracting metformin's glucose-lowering effect. May require diabetes medication adjustment.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood sugar more frequently. Dose adjustment of metformin may be needed.

interactions.description: Both cause drowsiness and CNS depression. Combined use may cause excessive sedation.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid driving or operating machinery. Consider using a less sedating antihistamine.

interactions.description: Aspirin may slightly reduce the blood-pressure-lowering effect of beta-blockers at high doses.
interactions.recommendation: Usually not clinically significant at low-dose aspirin (75-150mg). Monitor blood pressure.

interactions.description: Do NOT combine two ARBs. Dual ARB therapy provides no additional benefit but significantly increases risk of hypotension, hyperkalemia, and renal failure.
interactions.recommendation: NEVER use two ARBs together. Choose one.

interactions.description: Amoxicillin may increase INR and bleeding risk by affecting gut bacteria that produce vitamin K.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR during and after antibiotic course.

interactions.description: Both have serotonergic activity. Combined use increases risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination. Use non-serotonergic cough medication.

interactions.description: Ciprofloxacin can enhance the blood-sugar-lowering effect of glimepiride, causing severe hypoglycemia.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood sugar very frequently. Reduce glimepiride dose if needed.

interactions.description: Both have been associated with neuropsychiatric effects (mood changes, anxiety). Combined use may increase this risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for mood or behavioral changes. Report any new symptoms.
